name: War room
summary: A full page, the war room, that shows every running session as a small live terminal on a wall, grouped by project, in a layout you can add any widget to. Desktop only.
description: The war room is a page of its own, opened from the menu row, the c key in the menu or the link #warroom. Its wall shows one small read-only terminal per running session, grouped by project in the project colours, each with the session's status light and name. A tile connects only while it is on screen and repaints about once a second (four times a second under the pointer); hovering a tile scales it up and floats it over its neighbours without moving them, and a click opens the session. Four switches in the widget's header and menu add the extras, all remembered per browser: shells (off), browsers (off), asleep sessions (off, drawn as dimmed cards that wake the session when clicked) and paired computers (on, with an offline card while a link is down). The page is also the third one edit layout works on, after Home and the terminal page: drag any widget onto it beside the wall. The arrangement is saved on the server and is the same on every desktop. There is no war room on a phone: the menu row is hidden at 700 pixels wide and narrower.
where: The menu tab of the drawer: the war room row, under sessions (desktop only).
how_to: Open the drawer's menu tab and press the war room row, or press c while the menu has focus.
Hover a tile to enlarge it and refresh it faster; click it to open that session.

Drag the peek zoom slider in the widget header (or pick a stop in its menu) to set how big the hover peek is: the steps are equal from 0 (no zoom) to 100 (twice the default peek), the same peek width at every tile count. Resting tiles show the session's bottom rows filling the tile.
Use the shells, browsers, asleep and paired computers switches in the widget header (or its menu) to add or remove those tiles.
Press edit layout (right click on empty space, or the layout button) to open the widgets drawer on the war room.
Drag a widget, for example a stats tile, from the drawer onto the page; it is saved at once and kept after a reload.
Press reset in edit layout to put the page back to the wall alone.
examples: Open the war room on a second monitor and leave it there.
Turn on asleep, then click a dimmed card to wake that session.
Put the running sessions count and the providers widget beside the wall.
